Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Samira Ortiz (Head of Search, Aperture), Noah Kim (ML Engineer, Aperture), Dylan Price (Infra Lead, Aperture)

Summary:
Quick discovery on where to host embeddings + rerank. Aperture exploring hybrid search (BM25 + embed fanout + reranker), curious about Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs for latency/econ/compliance. Need benchmarks and network diagram; timeline target Q3 pilot.

Topics covered: hosting options, vector DB integration, embedding dims, rerank design (bi-encoder + cross-encoder), throughput and tail latency, caching strategies, security/VPC, cost levers.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Ethan our solutions engineer. Samira, Noah, Dylan, thanks for making time. quick agenda is: hear your current stack, constraints, and what success looks like.
[00:18] Samira (Aperture): Yeah thanks, im Samira. We run site search for apparel, about 45M SKUs across catalogs, lots of stale product descriptions and seasonal content, also user signals. We're looking to improve relevance with embeddings + rerank, but the thing is latency at checkout and search page needs to be tight, p95 under 120ms ideally.
[00:36] Maya: That p95 target is helpful. What's your current stack for retrieval?
[00:42] Noah: We use Elastic for BM25, Pinecone for a small pilot of embeddings, but that's not in prod. Pinecone costs exploded when we pushed more dims and fanout. Also, infra limits and we need SSO and SOC2 evidence for enterprise customers.
[00:58] Ethan (Redwood SE): Understood. A couple clarifying q's: what's your expected QPS and average fanout? and doc corpus size?
[01:07] Samira: Typical peak is 100 QPS for search endpoints, with heavy spikes during promos to 500 QPS. Fanout pre-rerank would be 50 candidates per query for initial experiments, maybe 20-30 if reranker is expensive. Corpus is ~200M text chunks, embeddings currently 512 dims in our pilot.
[01:32] Dylan (Aperture Infra): For security anything that touches PII needs to be in our VPC. We're leaning toward a Private deployment for compliance but want to understand econ vs Hosted and whether Dedicated reserved capacity can meet our throughput needs.
[01:48] Ethan: Good notes. High-level tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to integrate and cheapest to start but is multi-tenant. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower tail latency because you control GPU pool, and Private (VPC) is for networks and strict compliance—there's a platform fee and more setup.
[02:05] Maya: Also worth noting Redwood has automatic prefix caching and KV caching for LLM state which can cut per-request work if you have repeated prefixes or reranker contexts. That helps for cost and latency.
[02:18] Samira: Can you clarify the rerank piece — we were thinking bi-encoder embeddings for candidate retrieval then cross-encoder for final scoring. How does that map to cost?
[02:29] Ethan: Exactly that is the common pattern. Bi-encoder for fanout (cheap vector compare) then cross-encoder for rerank is higher quality but heavier per-call. We recommend tuning fanout size vs cross-encoder budget. Another option is a lightweight lexical+embedding hybrid score to reduce cross-encoder calls.
[02:47] Noah: For embeddings dims—our pilot used 512, but we saw Pinecone pricing go up with dims. Are smaller dims an option without losing recall?
[02:55] Ethan: Yes. 128 or 256 dims often give good tradeoffs for search; 512/768 improve fine-grained similarity but increase storage and compute. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and dimension reduction suggestions based on a sample workload.
[03:11] Dylan: If we go Private, will you run inside our VPC? what are the networking overheads for latency?
[03:19] Maya: For Redwood Private we offer a customer-managed VPC peering / private-link setup. Latency is largely network RTT plus model inference. If your search tier is in same region and we colocate inference pools, private path latency can be comparable to Hosted. There's initial setup and extra ops for certificate rotation and KMS integration.
[03:39] Samira: Anything we should know about vector DBs? We're considering embedding storage in Pinecone vs self-managed Milvus vs storing vectors in our infra + using Redwood as the inference layer.
[03:49] Ethan: Each has tradeoffs. Pinecone is managed but costs scale with dims and replica counts. Milvus gives more control but requires ops and sharding. Storing vectors yourselves and calling Redwood for embed and rerank means you control storage and can colocate, but you'd need to run the index cluster. Redwood supports standard vector DB connectors and can do hybrid search patterns (BM25 + embed fanout) with fallback routing.
[04:12] Noah: What about tail latency for fanout+rerank end-to-end? If we run cross-encoder for 50 candidates that could kill latency.
[04:20] Ethan: Right — common patterns to control tail latency: reduce fanout (20-30), use a fast lightweight reranker to filter to N candidates, then cross-encoder only on top 5-10. Also use batching and async priority queues for non-blocking background re-ranks. Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching and smart kernel selection to lower per-token overhead.
[04:48] Samira: Do you support hot prefix cache for frequent queries? We have a long tail but a small hot 5% of queries drive a lot of traffic.
[04:56] Maya: Yes, prefix caching and KV caching available in Dedicated and Private. Hosted also has caching but you can get more control in Dedicated (pinning cache entries, config TTLs).
[05:06] Dylan: On security we need KMS + HSM options and audit logs for compliance. Also SAML SSO for the console.
[05:14] Maya: We integrate with KMS providers and have audit logs; Private gives you HSM integrations and dedicated audit retention. We'll send the SOC2 docs and a security FAQ after the call.
[05:23] Samira: Great. One question on benchmarks — can you produce a throughput/lantency breakdown per model family? Our ML team wants numbers for 512-d vs 256-d embeddings with 100 qps and 50 fanout.
[05:35] Ethan: We can. We'll run a targeted benchmark for that configuration and provide a spreadsheet showing p50/p95/p99 and cost per million queries under Hosted/Dedicated/Private assumptions.
[05:44] Noah: What about quantized embeddings? we read about 8-bit or product quantization to save memory — any effect on recall for our catalog?
[05:53] Ethan: Quantization reduces precision and can slightly affect recall, but for many search workloads PQ or 8-bit works well. Redwood Optimize can recommend a quantization profile after sampling your dataset. We usually test offline eval sets to ensure recall meets threshold before rolling to prod.
[06:10] Samira: Timeline — we'd like to run a Q3 pilot and then decide by mid-Q3. Any blockers for a pilot?
[06:18] Maya: No major blockers. For Private we need a networking window with your infra team and about 2-4 weeks setup. Dedicated reserved capacity can be started faster if you want guaranteed capacity for the pilot. Hosted is immediate.
[06:29] Dylan: If we start with Hosted for quick iteration but want Private later, is migration smooth?
[06:35] Ethan: Yes migration is supported. Models and configs can be pinned and rollout policies transfer. We recommend testing with the same model family across environments to minimize regressions.
[06:44] Samira: Cost control — we need predictable unit economics. How do you help?
[06:50] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggests batching, caching, model quantization, and routing rules (route cheaper model variants for low-value queries). Console shows token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards so you can monitor.
[07:05] Noah: Can we do hybrid search where we run BM25 first and only call embeddings if BM25 score below threshold? That could cut cost.
[07:12] Ethan: Absolutely. Hybrid routing is common: lexical-first, then dense retrieval for fallback or augmentation. Redwood supports conditional routing and fallback to reduce cross-encoder calls.
[07:24] Samira: Regarding metrics for success: we want improvement in click-through and conversion, but for pilot we'll use p95 latency <120ms and relevance lift on A/B of +6% CTR.
[07:36] Maya: Noted. We'll capture those as success criteria in follow-up docs.
[07:42] Dylan: One more infra detail — we need TLS termination inside our VPC and private IPs; will Redwood support internal-only endpoints?
[07:50] Maya: Private supports private endpoints and internal TLS certs. We'll include network diagram and required firewall rules in the packet we send.
[08:00] Samira: Any recommended embedding dim for apparel search specifically? brand/visual features vs text?
[08:07] Ethan: Apparel often benefits from mid-sized dims (128-256) for faster similarity and good recall if you also use product metadata signals. If you plan to merge image embeddings, you may need 512 or specialized joint embeddings.
[08:22] Noah: We also want the ability to run local rerank models on cheap CPU for baseline and offload heavy cross-encoder to GPU pools.
[08:30] Ethan: That pattern works: run a small CPU-based lightweight reranker or pointwise model, and offload the cross-encoder to GPU-backed Dedicated/Private pools when needed. Redwood can route to different model families by policy.
[08:45] Samira: Let's talk numbers — do you have rough cost per million queries for Hosted vs Dedicated for our config (100 qps, 50 fanout, 512 dims)?
[08:55] Maya: We'll include an estimate in the pricing packet; rough order numbers: Hosted entry cost lower but scales with dims and storage; Dedicated gives lower per-query compute if you commit capacity. Exact numbers depend on embedding size, storage, and rerank frequency. We'll run the benchmark and provide numbers.
[09:09] Noah: For the benchmark we can provide 10k sample queries and label set, would that help?
[09:15] Ethan: Perfect — that'll let us compute recall/precision and tune dims/quantization suggestions.
[09:21] Samira: Any compliance gotchas for EU data residency? We have EU customers and need some data at rest inside region.
[09:27] Maya: Redwood Hosted has region controls for EU, Dedicated/Private can be deployed in EU regions or on-prem if needed. We'll note data residency options in follow-up.
[09:37] Dylan: Are there any connectors for existing vector DBs—like if we keep Milvus can Redwood read/write to it?
[09:43] Ethan: Yes, we have connectors and can integrate with common vector indexes; we can also point your index to use Redwood-inferred embeddings and serve rerank.
[09:51] Samira: Ok last thing — operational fallback. During spikes can Redwood degrade gracefully? we don't want errors at peak traffic.
[09:58] Ethan: Redwood has routing rules—automatic fallback to cheaper model variants, region fallback, and queuing policies. In Dedicated you can configure burst capacity to cover spikes.
[10:12] Maya: Alright i think we have enough to follow up. quick recap of next steps?
[10:18] Samira: Yes, please send security docs, pricing, and benchmark plan. we'll share sample queries.
[10:23] Maya: We'll do that. Ethan will prepare the benchmark config and I'll send pricing + network diagram. schedule deep-dive for infra the week of 6/29.
[10:33] Noah: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:36] Dylan: Thanks.
[10:38] Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.
